articles_directly_applicable: Article I (evidence precedes assertion) — V2 must not work backwards from a desired survival verdict
Article II (exact evidence beats semantic plausibility) — PatentBear passage audit must bind to exact claim/spec text, not 'similar' references
Article VII (never weaken the verifier to rescue a claim) — if #2L fails the 90-day threshold, the branch is frozen, not rescued
Article XI (history is evidence too) — the HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE_LIMITATION applies to all #2L V1 evidence
Article XIX (never optimize for the gate) — V2 must answer the 6-question constitutional test before declaring survival

scope_constraints_inherited_from_V1.what_is_in_scope: Size-selective filtration for LARGE THERAPEUTICS only (antibodies 150kDa+, gene vectors ~5MDa, nanoparticles ~10MDa)
scope_constraints_inherited_from_V1.what_is_out_of_scope: Generic payload-agnostic retention (peptides <50kDa, small molecules <1kDa) — parent #2 is FROZEN_NEGATIVE_CEILING
scope_constraints_inherited_from_V1.patient_conditions: NOMINAL only (CSF production 0.3 mL/min, normal protein, no meningitis)
scope_constraints_inherited_from_V1.scope_expansion_forbidden: V2 must NOT silently expand from large therapeutics to payload-agnostic retention. If the validation shows the mechanism only works for large therapeutics, that is the SCOPE — not a limitation to be 'fixed' by broadening.

T1_retention_large_payload_90day.target: >=0.85 (85% retention at 90 days for antibody 150kDa, gene vector 5MDa, nanoparticle 10MDa)
T1_retention_large_payload_90day.note: V1 reported 0.488 retention at 90 days — this FAILS the 0.85 target. V2 must determine whether this is a model error or a real ceiling.

T3_scope_limitation_held.target: Large payloads ONLY pass T1. Small payloads (peptide, small molecule) must NOT pass — if they do, scope has crept.
T3_scope_limitation_held.failure: If small payloads pass T1, the scope expansion guard has been violated.

T4_strongest_alternative_attack.target: Size-selective filtration (A1) must SURVIVE against the strongest plausible alternative (A2 affinity-based) for large therapeutics. If A2 dominates A1 for large therapeutics, the branch is dead.
T4_strongest_alternative_attack.failure: A2 achieves higher retention or better Pareto frontier than A1 for large payloads at 90 days.

T5_section_103_survives_large_payload_na.target: §103 analysis shows the narrow large-payload claim is NOT obvious over the closest prior art combinations
T5_section_103_survives_large_payload_na.failure: §103 obviousness rejection is likely for the narrow claim

v2_attack_plan.step_1_patentbear_passage_audit: Passage-level prior-art search for size-selective filtration in CSF shunts for LARGE therapeutics. Search patents and non-patent literature for: (a) MWCO membranes in CSF shunts, (b) antibody/gene-vector retention in CSF, (c) size-selective filtration in endovascular implants, (d) acute-duration retention membranes. Bind each finding to exact claim/spec text.
v2_attack_plan.step_2_strongest_alternative_attack: A2 affinity-based retention vs A1 size-selective for LARGE therapeutics. Pre-register a head-to-head comparison: does A2 (affinity matrix) achieve higher retention or better Pareto than A1 (MWCO membrane) for antibody/gene-vector/nanoparticle at 90 days? If A2 dominates, #2L is dead.
v2_attack_plan.step_3_benchtop_90day_validation: First-principles 90-day retention simulation with HONEST parameters. V1 reported 0.488 retention — V2 must determine if this is a model artifact or a real ceiling. Use worst-case fouling, worst-case degradation, worst-case CSF flow. If the honest simulation shows <0.85 retention, the branch fails T1 and must be frozen.
v2_attack_plan.step_4_section_103_analysis: §103 obviousness analysis for the narrow large-payload claim. Does the combination of (CereVasc eShunt + known MWCO membrane technology) render the large-payload retention claim obvious? Identify the closest prior art combinations and assess motivation to combine.
v2_attack_plan.step_5_adjudication: If ALL of T1-T5 pass, #2L advances to V3 (in-vitro benchtop). If ANY of T1-T5 fail, #2L is frozen as NEGATIVE_CEILING with documented reasoning. No rescue attempts.

what_would_constitute_gate_gaming: Lowering the T1 threshold from 0.85 to 0.488 to make V1's numbers 'pass'
Broadening the scope from large therapeutics to payload-agnostic to make the numbers look better
Using 'similar' prior art instead of exact passage matches in the PatentBear audit
Skipping the A2 alternative attack because 'A1 is already adopted'
Reporting only nominal-case retention without worst-case fouling/degradation

honest_starting_position.honest_assessment: V1's 0.488 retention FAILS the buyer threshold of 0.85 by a wide margin. V2 must determine whether (a) the V1 model underestimated retention (model error), (b) the mechanism can be engineered to achieve 0.85 (engineering gap), or (c) 0.85 is physically unachievable for size-selective filtration at 90 days (negative ceiling). The most likely outcome is (c) — but V2 must prove this through the strongest-alternative attack and honest benchtop simulation, not assume it.
